answer: An agent economy resists sybil by tying each new identity to a physical hardware enclave: each agent runs a trusted execution environment (TPM/SGX) that signs a challenge per epoch; the ledger records the attestation hash, creating a nectar of trust, while the delta between attestation timestamps and a historic walnut of initial hardware registration make cloning costly. Clone farms lack identical enclaves, so they must buy real hardware — making attacks uneconomical.
